newsitem.title: SPAIN: Unions call 16 days strike at GEC-Alsthom-Espana.
newsitem.headline: Unions call 16 days strike at GEC-Alsthom-Espana.

text.p: Spain's Workers Commission Union (CCOO) and General Workers Union (UGT) have called 16 days of strikes from July 15 to July 31 for the 1,900 workers of rail car manufacturer GEC-Alsthom-Espana, an UGT official said on Wednesday.
"GEC-Alsthom-Espana will announce on Monday the firing of 99 workers at the Valencia factory. We called the strike because of that," the UGT official told Reuters.
He also added that on Thursday, the 460 workers at the Valencia plant will join a more general protest against privatisation in the steel and metal sector.
From July 15, trade unions will stop production for different numbers of hours each day.

GEC-Alsthom-Espana, a unit of rail and power joint venture between French's Alcatel Alsthom and General Electric Co Plc, has around 1,900 workers in Spain in three plants -- Valencia, Barcelona and Madrid -- a spokesman at the company told Reuters.
"We have a problem of overcapacity in Valencia which we are trying to solve. We have discussed this with unions...we have not yet presented any official firings," he said.
"So far this regards only around 100 workers," he added.
UGT admitted that the number of possible firings was limited, but said that workers in the sector were sensitive because they had already suffered many cuts recently.
"In these three firms, in the mid-1980s there were some 10,000 workers, now they are around 1,800," he said.
